title: The Denver Endgame Squeeze
description: Robert James Fischer faces Bent Larsen in Game 5 of the 1971 Candidates semifinal match in Denver. The game opens with Sicilian tension, but the real story is how activity slowly becomes a lasting endgame edge. Watch the rook invasion, the bishop trades, and the final pawn race where one tempo decides everything. This game stands out as a practical lesson in turning pressure into a win.

But Black's king is tied to the queening square, and White has the opposition. Fischer finds the final king move: {{m:91}}. Larsen realized his position was lost, and resigned. The result is one to zero for Robert James Fischer.

This game matters because Fischer turns a balanced Sicilian into a lesson in rook activity, king activity, and timing. No final attack is needed, just pressure that keeps improving until the pawn race is hopeless for Black.
